data.title: U.S. Sanctions and Threatens to Dismantle International Criminal Court — WSJ
data.description:
By Matthew Dalton, Vera Bergengruen and Laurence Norman

PARIS — The Trump administration announced sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court on Friday, threatening to dismantle the institution after it issued an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The announcement comes on the day that Navi Pillay, a South African former ICC judge, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. The committee cited her "efforts to promote peace and international law."

The sanctions could deal a potentially crippling blow to the ICC by cutting it off from the U.S. financial system and prohibiting it from conducting transactions in dollars. Western banks often refuse to deal at all with sanctioned entities, because of the difficulty of separating their dollar trades from transactions in other major currencies.

"Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a video Friday, arguing that the court threatens American sovereignty by threatening to prosecute U.S. citizens despite Washington never having joined it.

The sanctions allow a grace period of six months, which officials said could give time to craft a deal that would address U.S. concerns. U.S. officials are seeking guarantees that the court won't target U.S. citizens. They have also criticized the court's stance that it can prosecute citizens of nonmember states, a group that includes the U.S., Israel and Russia.

Reining in that authority, however, would likely require the court's member states to amend the Rome Statute, the founding treaty of the ICC. The statute allows the court to prosecute nonmember state nationals if they commit war crimes and crimes against humanity on the territory of member states. The court's backers consider that provision a fundamental principle of international criminal law.

The ICC has used that authority to prosecute Netanyahu for alleged war crimes on Palestinian territory, which is considered a court member state, and Russian President Vladimir Putin for alleged crimes in Ukraine. It has also allowed the court to investigate alleged crimes committed by Central Intelligence Agency officials and the U.S. military in Afghanistan.

Washington informed European capitals of the decision on Thursday. Rubio issued a warning to them and other U.S. allies that belong to the court. "We expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ICC and that rely on American servicemembers for their defense, to rein in this rogue court," he said.

The ICC said it wouldn't be deterred by the U.S. sanctions.

"The court will continue to fully discharge its mandate, with independence and impartiality, acting only on the basis of law and the evidence, for the sake of the countless victims of grave crimes," said ICC President Tomoko Akane.

The ICC, based in The Hague, is heir to the Nuremberg tribunals that prosecuted Nazi war criminals after World War II and special courts that held trials after the Yugoslav wars and the Rwandan genocide. European governments and human rights groups view it as a key institution for enforcing international law, even though the world's most powerful and populous nations — the U.S., China, India and Russia — aren't members.

The U.S. already has sanctioned a number of ICC officials. They include former Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan, whom the ICC ousted in July over sexual-assault allegations against him; Akane and several other judges; the court's two deputy prosecutors; and the lead prosecutor in the case against Netanyahu and other Israeli officials. Khan has denied any sexual misconduct.

The sanctions announced Friday are far more punitive, applying to the institution as a whole. The court has been bracing for the move for months. It has paid employees through the end of the year and switched away from Microsoft to a German open source software system.

The Dutch government, which hosts the ICC, and other court member states have vowed to defend the institution.

The European Union called the U.S. decision "deeply regrettable" and pledged to work with the ICC to ensure it continues to operate effectively.

Some officials have suggested the EU could use a so-called blocking statute to prevent EU-based banks or businesses from complying with the sanctions. The EU said it stands ready "to take any necessary measures" to allow the court to keep working.

Write to Matthew Dalton at Matthew.Dalton@wsj.com, Vera Bergengruen at vera.bergengruen@wsj.com and Laurence Norman at laurence.norman@wsj.com

data.title: US FDA approves Asahi Kasei's drug for persistent herpes infections
data.description:
The US FDA on Friday approved Japan's Asahi Kasei's drug for persistent herpes simplex virus sores in certain patients with weakened immune systems who have not responded to available antiviral treatments.

  • The oral drug, called pritelivir, was developed by German drugmaker Aicuris, which Asahi Kasei acquired in April

  • Pritelivir blocks proteins the herpes virus needs to copy its genetic material, stopping it from multiplying and allowing the drug to work against some infections resistant to older treatments

  • Older first-line drugs must be activated by a viral enzyme before blocking replication, and mutations that disrupt this activation can cause resistance

  • The US Food and Drug Administration's approval was based on a late-stage trial involving 101 participants, in which sores healed completely within 28 days in 62.7% of patients who were given pritelivir, compared to 34% receiving other treatments

  • The trial compared pritelivir with doctors' choice of intravenous foscarnet, the main approved alternative, or cidofovir and imiquimod — older medicines used off-label

  • The commonly reported side effects in the trial included headache, diarrhea, nausea, reduced appetite, vomiting and dizziness

  • Asahi Kasei had previously estimated pritelivir could serve about 15,000 US patients with weakened immune systems, and generate peak annual sales of more than $400 million in the mid-to-late 2030s

data.title: Tesla Supplier Simwon America Files for IPO — Update
data.description:
By Josh Beckerman

Simwon America, which provides parts for Tesla, filed for an initial public offering.

The company expects to sell 1.5 million shares and expects stockholders to offer 1 million, with an expected price range of $18 to $22 each.

The Lathrop, Calif., company's indirect parent companies MS Autotech Co., Ltd. and Myoung Shin Industry Co., Ltd. are listed in Korea.

Simwon America is seeking a Nasdaq Global Market listing under symbol SWA.

The company focuses on "Body-in-White" components.

In the risk factor section of its IPO filing, Simwon America notes that "we currently derive substantially all of our revenue from Tesla." For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, sales to Tesla accounted for about 99.5% of total revenue.

For the year ended June 30, 2026, revenue was down 13% to $323.9 million as "growth in the electric vehicle market moderated compared to prior periods."

The company has a 277,208-square-foot assembly facility and 198,183-square-foot fabrication facility in Lathrop. It plans to use some IPO proceeds to buy a company on the East Coast to support expansion and for expansion initiatives targeting the Mexican and Canadian markets.

Write to Josh Beckerman at josh.beckerman@wsj.com

data.title: US measles cases rise to 4,080, CDC says
data.description:
The US CDC on Friday reported 4,080 confirmed measles cases in the country as of October 8, up 193 from a week earlier.

Here are key details:

  • Twenty-six cases were identified among international visitors, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

  • Measles-related hospitalizations this year stand at 414, or 10% of cases, compared with 244 hospitalizations in 2025

  • The CDC has confirmed two measles-associated deaths in 2026, though it has not identified the states involved, compared with three deaths in 2025

  • Separately, Pennsylvania health officials have reported five deaths linked to the state's measles outbreak this year

  • Last month, the CDC shifted to using mortality data from the National Center for Health Statistics for measles-related deaths, rather than relying on state health departments, a change that has drawn scrutiny

  • As of October 9, the Pennsylvania health department has reported 1,136 measles cases in 2026, including 219 hospitalizations

  • Children and teenagers aged 5 to 19 accounted for the largest share of cases at 1,716, or 42% of infections, followed by adults aged 20 and older at 1,635 cases, or 40%

  • Earlier this week, New York declared a statewide disaster emergency over a measles outbreak after reporting 108 cases this year through October 3, including 92 cases since July 15

data.title: Bitcoin holder loses 80 BTC worth $5.2 million after moving funds to reseller-bought Ledger
data.description:
A Bitcoin holder watched 80 BTC, worth $5.2 million, vanish after moving the coins onto a Ledger hardware wallet. The device was not bought from Ledger directly. It came from CryptoBilis, a reseller operating in Southeast Asia.

The transfer to the new device happened just one week before the funds disappeared.

The 80 BTC loss is not an isolated case. Multiple buyers who purchased Ledger devices through the same reseller have reported significant losses.

Ledger confirmed on October 9, 2026, that it is investigating fund losses connected to CryptoBilis. The company is not waiting for the investigation to finish before issuing guidance.

Anyone who bought a Ledger from the reseller in the last 90 days has been told not to initialize their device. Ledger is also advising those buyers to move their assets to new Ledger wallets set up with different seed phrases.

Another victim reported losing 7 million USDT, a dollar-pegged stablecoin. That user had bought a Ledger device three weeks before the incident.

On-chain analysts have tracked assets flowing to theft addresses across several blockchain networks. Trackers have identified $17.7 million in BTC and $29 million worth of ETH equivalents sitting in wallets linked to the thefts.

Analysts' estimates of the total damage range from $72 million to over $87 million, spread across numerous victim wallets.

The cause has not been confirmed. Speculation centers on two possibilities: supply-chain tampering, where a device is compromised before it reaches the buyer, or phishing attacks that trick users into handing over sensitive information.

So far, no reports indicate that Ledger devices bought through official channels have been affected. That points toward a localized issue tied to CryptoBilis.

The reseller's footprint covers Southeast Asian markets including Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines.

If supply-chain tampering turns out to be the cause, the security model breaks down if someone gets to the hardware first. If phishing is behind the losses, the takeaway shifts toward user behavior and how victims were targeted.

For now, the practical steps are straightforward. Anyone who bought a Ledger from CryptoBilis in the past 90 days should follow the company's guidance: do not initialize the device, and move funds to a new Ledger wallet with a different seed phrase.

Ledger's investigation will need to determine what actually happened, whether the reseller was complicit or itself a victim, and whether the damage extends beyond the current estimates.

data.title: OPay, Digital Financial Platform For Emerging Markets, Files for NYSE IPO
data.description:
OPay Limited filed an F-1 to list American Depositary Shares on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker "OPAY." The Nigeria-focused, Singapore-headquartered fintech plans a concurrent private placement with Stanbic Africa Holdings of up to $200 million (or a formula-based amount). As an emerging growth company, OPay will use proceeds for technology, market expansion, and potential acquisitions.

Business Description

OPay is a digital financial platform built for emerging markets that provides consumers and merchants with payments, money management, and credit solutions. Its core consumer offerings include a mobile wallet, cashless payments (online and offline), bill pay, and savings products offered through a licensed microfinance bank in Nigeria, with deposit protection provided by the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation. On the merchant side, OPay enables payment acceptance via POS devices, QR and app-based tools, online checkout (“Pay with OPay”), and provides settlement, reconciliation, and business tools. The company also offers credit: self-originated consumer and merchant loans in Nigeria and loan facilitation in Indonesia through a locally licensed entity operated via contractual arrangements (VIE).

OPay generates revenue primarily from transaction-based services (payments and acquiring), loan financing services (interest on self-originated loans), loan facilitation services (fees net of lender and insurance costs), and interest income from short-term investments supporting its savings products. The platform is designed for reliability in low-connectivity environments and entry-level devices, and applies AI-driven risk analytics for fraud prevention and underwriting, which the company cites as key competitive strengths.

Market Overview

  • Total addressable market: Large, underpenetrated financial services markets in Nigeria and Egypt with significant unbanked and cash-reliant populations.
  • Market growth: Nigeria real GDP ~4.0% in 2025; Egypt ~4.4% in 2025; rising internet and smartphone penetration through 2030.
  • Market position: No. 1 finance app in Africa & Middle East by MAU (9.9%) and among the largest processors of digital payments/transfers in Nigeria (Frost & Sullivan).
  • Key competitors: Traditional banks, digital banks, mobile money operators, and lending-focused fintechs.
  • Industry trends: Rapid shift from cash to digital, growth in POS acceptance, real-time payments infrastructure, and supportive regulatory frameworks.

Operational Metrics

  • Customers: 50.1 million MAU and 26.8 million DAU as of July 31, 2026; DAU/MAU ratio of 54%
  • Locations: Principal operations in Nigeria, Indonesia, Egypt and Pakistan
  • Geographic presence: Nigeria (core), Indonesia (loan facilitation), Egypt (merchant acquiring), Pakistan (merchant acquiring and consumer wallet)
  • Partnerships: Memorandum of understanding with Stanbic Africa Holdings (Standard Bank Group) for strategic collaboration
  • Orders/GMV: 90.1 billion transactions and US$558 billion GTV for the 12 months ending June 30, 2026; H1 2026 GTV of US$339.1 billion
  • Other key metrics: 6.7 million total quarterly unique borrowers in Nigeria (Q2 2026); US$1.56 billion Nigerian loan origination (LTM to June 30, 2026); 0.8 million active POS terminals (June 2026); 38.7 million OPay Debit Cards issued (June 30, 2026); over 42 million savings subscribers with ~US$23 average balance; NPL ratio 4.3% (June 30, 2026); CAC (ex-Indonesia) US$1.9 in H1 2026

Financials Highlights

  • Revenue (current): US$536.3 million (FY 2025)
  • Revenue growth: Up 160.7% vs. 2024 (US$205.7 million)
  • Operating income: US$107.1 million (FY 2025); US$131.2 million (H1 2026)
  • Net income: US$72.5 million (FY 2025); US$90.9 million (H1 2026)

Management

  • James Zhou, Non-Executive Chairman; Founder - Founder of Opera Limited and Kunlun Tech; tech entrepreneur with extensive emerging market experience.
  • Lars Rahbaek Boilesen, Executive Director, Co-CEO - Former CEO of Opera Software; senior leadership roles across digital and payments businesses.
  • Stephen Wen, Co-CEO and COO; Executive Director Nominee - Former Ant Group executive and founding CEO of Alipay Hong Kong; 15+ years in fintech and digital banking.
  • James Arthur Perry Jr, Chief Financial Officer - Former Head of Asia Pacific Technology Investment Banking at Citigroup; veteran capital markets banker.
  • Trond Riiber Knudsen, Independent Director - Founder/CEO of TRK Group; former senior partner at McKinsey & Company.

IPO Structure

  • Issuer: OPay Limited
  • Filing date: October 09, 2026
  • Proposed ticker: OPAY
  • Exchange: NYSE
  • Lead underwriters: Citigroup, Deutsche Bank, Standard Bank, CICC; co-managers: B. Riley Securities, Needham & Company
  • Use of proceeds: General corporate purposes, including investments in technology, distribution, new solutions, market expansion, and potential acquisitions or strategic investments.

Original SEC Filing: OPAY Ltd - F-1 - Oct. 09, 2026
